summary: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in JanuaryMost footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross.

Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024, the midfielder entered – and won – a running race.Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds.
He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor.

stories.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
summary: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded.
Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era?For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture.

Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport.As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico’s relevance.

summary: AFC president Sheikh Salman praises and hugs InfantinoIt had stood with Uefa and Concacaf against himThe Asian Football Confederation has endorsed Gianni Infantino for another term as Fifa’s president in a turnaround in its stance from two months ago when it criticised the head of football’s world governing body for a breach of trust.The AFC president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, speaking at the body’s extraordinary congress in Tokyo on Friday, embraced Infantino with a large hug in front of the membership as he delivered his endorsement.

stories.title: Chess: Bodhana Sivanandan, 11, can break another world age record on Friday
summary: England’s talent from Harrow can become the youngest female international master in chess historyBodhana Sivanandan, 11, who needed just a few rating points to qualify for an open international master title and to break Judit Polgar’s world age record, went very close to a draw against the former world title challenger GM Aleksandra Goryachkina in round one of this week’s European Club Cup, then outplayed her IM opponent in round three to take her rating to 2399.4 against the 2400 needed.

In her next game, she drew from a winning position against GM Nino Batsiashvili, rated 2426.Sivanandan has thus already joined the 10 youngest 2400-rated players of all time, who include the new Russian star Roman Shogdzhiev, the world No 5, Nodirbek Abdusattorov, Argentina’s Faustino Oro, and Turkey’s Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus.
